brief: A third-party write-up of a Goldman Sachs Delta One desk note by Rich Privorotsky, who says OpenAI's Astra looks like it matters. SoftBank rose over 10% overnight as an OpenAI proxy and Oracle gained about 5.5%, but the note treats the price moves as the least interesting part. The argument: a leading model stepping away from the pack is the outcome the AI bull case needed, because meaningfully smarter models make companies find new uses rather than buy the same amount of AI cheaper, which forces rival labs to chase and keeps the spending cycle from going stale. Privorotsky says his prior comment on token demand growth lagging token cost declines was taken out of context. His stated position was conditional: more demand plus lower prices is not automatically bullish if pricing falls faster than consumption grows, and compute oversupply becomes plausible unless capability keeps making radical jumps. He clarifies it was not a bearish AI call while acknowledging the hardware complex has cheapened relative to earnings. Greg Brockman called Astra a generational leap, though no agreed-upon AGI test exists. September calendar seen as helpful, with Oracle reporting next week.
